title: Jacobson-radical completion of a Noetherian semilocal ring
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring] whose distinct maximal ideals are $\mathfrak m_1,\ldots,\mathfrak m_t$, with $0\leq t<\infty$. Put $J=\bigcap_{i=1}^t\mathfrak m_i$, taking the empty intersection to be $A$, and put $C=\varprojlim_{n\geq1}A/J^n$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion]. For each $i$ let $H_i=\varprojlim_{n\geq1} A_{\mathfrak m_i}/(\mathfrak m_iA_{\mathfrak m_i})^n$, using localization at a prime [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. The canonical maps induced by $A\to A_{\mathfrak m_i}$ give an isomorphism of $A$-algebras $C\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_{i=1}^tH_i$. In particular each factor map agrees on $A$ with localization followed by completion. For $t=0$, $A$ and both sides are the zero ring.

source.place: Tag 07N9, algebra-lemma-completion-finite-extension, proof: decomposition of the completion of a semilocal algebra into completed local factors. The same Chinese-remainder/inverse-limit argument applies to an arbitrary Noetherian semilocal ring at its Jacobson radical, without a chosen finite map from a local base.

proof.text: If $t=0$, the maximal-ideal existence assertion of [lem-weil-pbc-proper-ideal-contained-in-maximal] implies that $A$ is the zero ring. Then $J=A$, each $A/J^n$ is zero, and the empty product is the zero ring. This proves every clause in this case. Henceforth $t>0$.

For $i\ne j$, maximality and distinctness give $\mathfrak m_i+\mathfrak m_j=A$: otherwise the sum, containing $\mathfrak m_i$, would equal $\mathfrak m_i$ and force $\mathfrak m_j=\mathfrak m_i$. Choose $u\in\mathfrak m_i$, $v\in\mathfrak m_j$ with $u+v=1$. For $n\ge1$, expand $1=(u+v)^{2n-1}$. Every term lies in $\mathfrak m_i^n$ or $\mathfrak m_j^n$, so these powers are pairwise comaximal. Here comaximal means that the sum of the ideals is $A$.

source.place: Tag 00DT (algebra-lemma-chinese-remainder), with Tag 07N9 (algebra-lemma-completion-finite-extension), proof, quotient-product and inverse-limit argument.

proof.text: For ideals $K,L$ with $a+b=1$, $a\in K$, $b\in L$, an element $x\in K\cap L$ satisfies $x=xa+xb\in KL$, proving $K\cap L=KL$. For pairwise comaximal $I_1,\ldots,I_r$, their product up to $r-1$ is comaximal with $I_r$: multiply equations $a_j+b_j=1$ with $a_j\in I_j$, $b_j\in I_r$ to obtain $1-\prod_{j<r}a_j\in I_r$. Inducting from the one-ideal case therefore gives $\bigcap I_i=\prod I_i$. Apply this first to $\mathfrak m_i$, then to their powers from Step 2. Distributing finite products gives $J^n=(\prod_i\mathfrak m_i)^n=\prod_i\mathfrak m_i^n=\bigcap_i\mathfrak m_i^n$. This uses only the definition of ideal multiplication as finite sums of products.

source.place: Tag 00DT (algebra-lemma-chinese-remainder), with Tag 07N9 (algebra-lemma-completion-finite-extension), proof, quotient-product and inverse-limit argument.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pc-crt-ideal-quotient-product] to the finite pairwise comaximal ideals $\mathfrak m_i^n$ and use Step 3. It yields a ring isomorphism $\phi_n:A/J^n\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_i A/\mathfrak m_i^n$, sending the class of $a$ to its residue classes. This is an $A$-algebra isomorphism because its formula commutes with the structural maps from $A$. For the transition from $n+1$ to $n$, both composites send $[a]$ to $([a]\bmod\mathfrak m_i^n)_i$; every class has such a representative. Thus the $\phi_n$ commute with transitions.

source.place: Tag 00DT (algebra-lemma-chinese-remainder), with Tag 07N9 (algebra-lemma-completion-finite-extension), proof, quotient-product and inverse-limit argument.

proof.text: Fix $i$ and $n\ge1$, and put $\mathfrak m=\mathfrak m_i$. If $s\notin\mathfrak m$, maximality gives $as+b=1$ for some $a\in A$, $b\in\mathfrak m$. Modulo $\mathfrak m^n$, the element $a(1+b+\cdots+b^{n-1})$ is an inverse for $s$, since their product is $1-b^n$. Thus every denominator in $A_{\mathfrak m}$ [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime] is already invertible modulo $\mathfrak m^n$. This construction uses no assertion that $A$ or $A/\mathfrak m^n$ is a domain.

source.place: Tag 00DT (algebra-lemma-chinese-remainder), with Tag 07N9 (algebra-lemma-completion-finite-extension), proof, quotient-product and inverse-limit argument.

proof.text: The extended ideal $(\mathfrak mA_{\mathfrak m})^n$ equals $\mathfrak m^nA_{\mathfrak m}$: expanding products of fractions proves one inclusion, and a generator $(x_1\cdots x_n)/s$ is a product of $n$ elements of $\mathfrak mA_{\mathfrak m}$, proving the other. Its elements are fractions $c/s$ with $c\in\mathfrak m^n$, since a finite sum of these fractions has a common denominator and numerator still in $\mathfrak m^n$. Hence localization gives $\lambda_{i,n}:A/\mathfrak m_i^n\to A_{\mathfrak m_i}/(\mathfrak m_iA_{\mathfrak m_i})^n$. It is surjective: for $x/s$, choose the inverse $v$ of $s$ modulo $\mathfrak m_i^n$ from Step 5; its class equals that of $xv/1$. It is injective: if $x/1=c/s$ with $c\in\mathfrak m_i^n$, fraction equality gives $u(sx-c)=0$ for some $u\notin\mathfrak m_i$. Thus $usx\in\mathfrak m_i^n$; the classes of $u$ and $s$ are units by Step 5, forcing $x\in\mathfrak m_i^n$. This proves bijectivity directly from the fraction relation of [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime].

source.place: Tag 00DT (algebra-lemma-chinese-remainder), with Tag 07N9 (algebra-lemma-completion-finite-extension), proof, quotient-product and inverse-limit argument.

proof.text: Compose $\phi_n$ with the product of the $\lambda_{i,n}$ to obtain $\psi_n:A/J^n\xrightarrow{\sim}\prod_i A_{\mathfrak m_i}/(\mathfrak m_iA_{\mathfrak m_i})^n$. The maps $\lambda_{i,n}$ commute with reduction: both routes on a class $[a]$ give the class of $a/1$ at level $n$. Together with Step 4 this proves transition compatibility of $\psi_n$. By [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion], $C$ consists of compatible sequences $x=(x_n)$. Send $x$ to $((\psi_n(x_n)_i)_{n\ge1})_i$. Conversely, from $(h_i)_i\in\prod_iH_i$, set $x_n=\psi_n^{-1}((h_{i,n})_i)$. Transition compatibility and injectivity of $\psi_n$ imply that these $x_n$ are compatible. The two formulas are inverse and preserve ring operations componentwise, so define a ring isomorphism $C\cong\prod_iH_i$.

source.place: Tag 00DT (algebra-lemma-chinese-remainder), with Tag 07N9 (algebra-lemma-completion-finite-extension), proof, quotient-product and inverse-limit argument.

proof.text: For $a\in A$, its image in $C$ is $([a]\bmod J^n)_n$. The isomorphism of Step 7 sends this to $(([a/1]\bmod(\mathfrak m_iA_{\mathfrak m_i})^n)_n)_i$. This is exactly localization followed by completion in every factor, using [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion] and [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime]. Thus the constructed ring isomorphism respects the given $A$-algebra structures and has the stipulated factor maps.
